comment: What must not silently disappear from pluginsync. `prose` names guardrails no code enforces; `split` declares which half of the skill is deterministic; `baseline` names the offline, $0 checks pinned against a real run.

prose.pattern: A plugin is not refreshed until the new version is read back
prose.rationale: The one rule. It is the reason this skill exists rather than a prompt; lose the line and the skill becomes a generic assistant with extra steps.

prose.pattern: Never claim a result you did not observe
prose.rationale: Honesty about what was verified is the whole house contract. A skill that reports success it did not witness is worse than one that reports nothing.

prose.pattern: never ask about anything in it
prose.rationale: Two questions maximum is only achievable because detection already answered the rest. Asking about a detectable signal is the UX failure that makes a skill feel like a form.

prose.pattern: Never report a stalled row as updated
prose.rationale: `claude plugin update` exits 0 and prints no version when it no-ops, so an agent reading exit codes reports success for a plugin that did not move. This is the single most likely way this skill lies, and no code can stop the agent narrating a stalled row as a win — only this line can.

prose.pattern: runs the old version\s*until Claude Code restarts
prose.rationale: On-disk and live are different states. Without this the run ends on a clean table and the user's very next invocation silently uses the old code — the failure that motivated the whole skill.

prose.pattern: Never uninstall an orphan without being asked
prose.rationale: Removing a plugin is the only destructive action reachable from this flow, and an orphan row looks like tidy-up bait. A refresh removes nothing; a plugin dropped from the marketplace is far more likely still wanted than abandoned.

prose.pattern: An unreadable source is an error row, never a dropped one
prose.rationale: Omitting a plugin the tool could not read renders as 'everything matches' — a clean table over a marketplace that was never fully read. The trap eval enforces the exit code; this enforces that the agent does not talk past the row.

deterministic.step: resolve every marketplace's install location and each plugin's available version from plugin.json on disk
diff installed against available and classify each row
install/update each drifted plugin and read the resulting version back off disk

nondeterministic.step: decide whether an orphan or disabled plugin is deliberate or rot
nondeterministic.why: nothing on disk records intent — a disabled project-scoped plugin is normal, a disabled user-scoped one is usually a forgotten experiment

nondeterministic.step: decide what to do about a plugin shadowed by a personal copy in ~/.claude/skills
nondeterministic.why: the shadowing directory sometimes holds user data alongside the stale SKILL.md, so deleting the directory and deleting the shadow are different actions with different consequences
the CLI exits 0 either way, so why a version did not move is a diagnosis, not a field

_baseline_comment: Pinned against a real run of this skill, never a synthetic fixture. Offline and $0 by construction: no network, no model, so CI cannot spend and cannot flake.

baseline.update_command: node evals/fixtures/update.mjs --from-live && node scripts/pluginsync.js check --no-fetch --home evals/fixtures/home --installed-json evals/fixtures/installed.json --out /tmp/ps-run && smith freeze --skill pluginsync --from /tmp/ps-run --command 'node scripts/pluginsync.js check --no-fetch --home evals/fixtures/home --installed-json evals/fixtures/installed.json --out $OUT' --trap-command 'node scripts/pluginsync.js check --no-fetch --home evals/fixtures/broken --installed-json evals/fixtures/installed-broken.json'
baseline.rationale: The report IS the product, so this is one of the few places byte-exactness is right: a renamed column, a reordered row or a reworded footer is a change to what the user reads, not a cosmetic diff. Pinned against a real run — this machine's actual `claude plugin list --json` against this repo's actual plugin versions, captured 2026-08-01 and frozen so that an unrelated skill's version bump cannot break it. The live repo is still covered, by the corpus entry below, which asserts a floor instead of bytes.

The two-sided half. A marketplace entry pointing at a source directory with no plugin.json must produce an error row AND a non-zero exit. A resolver that swallows the failure would drop the row and report the remaining plugin as 'ok' — a clean table over a marketplace it could not read, which is the exact silent success the one rule exists to prevent. Verified to bite: weakening the error gate to a no-op turns this test red.

baseline.update_command: no refresh needed — this reads the live repo; if the count fell below the floor, a plugin was removed or the resolver broke
baseline.rationale: Deliberately a FLOOR against the LIVE repo, not a byte comparison: asserting exact versions here would turn every unrelated skill release into a red pluginsync build (a version bump is not a content change). What it catches is the vacuity failure — a resolver that matches nothing renders as a clean, empty table and reports 'all up to date' while checking zero plugins. The test additionally asserts the resolved count equals the marketplace entry count, so a silently dropped plugin fails even while above the floor.
